(Getty) Summary * Trades valued near $5,499 accounted for $7.7 million, or 57 percent, of the Kalshi ether perpetual-futures volume CoinDesk analyzed from Sept. 17 through Sept. 20. * Recurring fixed-dollar trades appeared on 43 of 46 sampled dates since June, suggesting automated trading and raising concerns that a small number of participants may be driving much of the market’s reported activity. * Kalshi’s public data does not identify the traders or establish any wrongdoing, and the exchange did not explain who produced the repeated trades or why their target values changed. A small number of repeating trade sizes accounted for more than half the value traded on Kalshi's bitcoin and ether perpetual-futures markets, according to a CoinDesk analysis of the exchange's public trade records. On the ether market, trades valued within $2 of $5,499 accounted for $7.7 million, or 57%, of the $13.5 million in transactions [CoinDesk analyzed](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Bm8sUNcmJ6NfSV_n18IooH-TyGBkVhRqNKh-3F-LsYM/edit?usp=sharing) from Sept. 17 through Sept. 20.
